entities.summary: The Basilica of Saint Maternus, also known as the Basilica of Our Lady is a minor basilica in Walcourt, in the Namur Province of Belgium. According to legend, an oratory was founded here by Maternus of Cologne, who also carved a Madonna to replace an earlier pagan idol. The church does in fact contain a wooden Madonna, albeit from 950 to 1020, but still one of the oldest preserved Marian devotional statues in Western Christianity. The church was consecrated in 1026. The presence of the Madonna and its allegedly miraculous properties led to the development of the church into a pilgrimage site during the Middle Ages.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basilica of Saint Maternus played a significant regional role in Western Christianity during the Middle Ages, attracting pilgrims and influencing Marian devotional practices. Its wooden Madonna, carved between 950-1020, remains one of the oldest preserved examples.
